title: Revision HQ 2.3: complete outstanding programs
sub: Worksheet for the 360° experience: Revision HQ 2.3
objectives: understand how robust programs are made
know which lessons I'm secure on and which to revise
starter: A school is about to publish an app written by students. List everything you would check before it goes live.

stations.name: Lesson 1: Input validation
stations.challenge: Explain what is meant by a length check and give an example.

logic.title: Which check would reject an empty username?
Which check ensures a score is between 0 and 100?
Which could crash a program even with valid input?

stations.name: Lesson 3: Maintainability
stations.challenge: Describe three ways a programmer can make their code easier to maintain.

logic.title: Which makes code easier to maintain?
What happens to comments when code runs?

stations.name: Lesson 4: Testing and errors
stations.challenge: Explain what is meant by the term iterative testing.

logic.title: A program runs but gives the wrong answer. What type of error is this?

stations.name: Lesson 5: Test data
stations.challenge: Suggest test data for an order form accepting quantities 1 to 10.

logic.title: A form accepts 1 to 10. Which is boundary data?
A form accepts 1 to 10. Which is erroneous data?
A form accepts 1 to 10. Which is invalid data?

stations.name: Plan a 12-mark answer
stations.challenge: Plan the points you would include in a long answer about producing robust programs.

logic.title: Which points belong in a 12-mark answer on producing robust programs? Select all that apply.
What makes a 12-mark answer stand out?

final.title: Final challenge: key terms
final.instr: write what each one matches with.

checklist: Security desk worksheet (L1): date of birth validation
Cyber defence HQ worksheet (L2): the password strength checker
Code clinic worksheet (L3): rewriting Exhibit A using good practice
Bug hunt lab worksheet (L4): every error in the total cost program
Test lab worksheet (L5): the comment box test plan
exam: A program will be used by hundreds of students. Explain the techniques a programmer should use to make it robust.
